title: Every tile figure equals the figure in its report
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an owner/admin (or any user with the Reports permission) on the build under test; a single workplace is selected.
  2. A workplace with data for Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization and Sales by Customer (seed invoiced work orders with labour and clocked hours through the app).
  3. To check a KPI tile against its report, open the matching report with all advisors/technicians selected and the same date range.
custom_steps:
1. For each measure, read the tile's figure for a date range, then open its matching report for the same workplace, date range and filters and read the same figure.
2. Confirm the tile and the report show the same number, and that they never disagree.
3. Note for the tester: proving there is no caching/staleness gap at the code level is a developer/automated check; by hand, confirm the two figures match whenever you compare them.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Every dashboard figure equals its matching report's figure for the same workplace, date range and filters, at every moment — any difference caused by one being computed more recently than the other is a defect, with no freshness allowance.
  • If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490, story SV-9575 (S3 — Measure Formulas & Report Parity); Dashboard v1 specification, Confluence page 788430850, section S3; read on 2 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3-N1: “If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
